import hashlib
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path.cwd()
BASE = Path('docs/audits/decision-index-repair-20261008')
OLD = Path('docs/audits/decision-index-scope-20261008')
sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT / 'scripts'), str(ROOT / 't/python')]
import decision_records as published
import decision_store_git as selected
from test_decision_production_growth import ProductionFixture, REGISTRY, AUTHORITIES


def need(condition, cause):
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(cause)


def pin(raw):
    return {'bytes': len(raw), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()}


def receipt(result):
    command = [str(value).replace(str(ROOT) + '/', '') for value in result.args]
    return {'command': command, 'status': result.returncode,
            'stdout': result.stdout.decode(), 'stderr': result.stderr.decode()}


def parse(raw, tree):
    need(raw.endswith(b'\0'), 'complete native inventory frame')
    result = {}
    for record in raw.split(b'\0')[:-1]:
        header, name = record.split(b'\t', 1)
        fields = header.decode().split()
        mode, oid = fields[0], fields[2] if tree else fields[1]
        need(name.decode() not in result, 'unique native path')
        result[name.decode()] = [mode, oid]
    return result


def main():
    diagnosis = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', str(OLD / 'verify.py')], capture_output=True)
    need(diagnosis.returncode == 0 and not diagnosis.stderr, 'immutable whole stock diagnosis qualification')
    prior = json.loads((OLD / 'proof.json').read_bytes())
    paths = [f'scripts/{name}.py' for name in
             ('decision_records', 'decision_store_git', 'decision_catalog', 'decision_store')]
    paths += ['t/python/test_decision_store_git.py', 't/python/test_decision_production_growth.py',
              str(BASE / 'qualify.py'), str(BASE / 'verify.py')]
    sources = {name: {'source': Path(name).read_text(), 'identity': pin(Path(name).read_bytes())}
               for name in paths}
    fixture = ProductionFixture()
    try:
        for path in paths[:4]:
            fixture.write(path, Path(path).read_bytes())
        fixture.git('add', 'scripts')
        fixture.git('commit', '-q', '-m', 'fixture complete current scoped reader')
        data = {name: (fixture.root / name).read_bytes() for name in fixture.original_products}
        changed = {'scripts/decision_records.py', 'scripts/decision_store_git.py'}
        need(set(data) == set(prior['complete_before']), 'complete unchanged input membership')
        need(all(pin(raw) == prior['complete_before'][name] for name, raw in data.items()
                 if name not in changed), 'complete non-repair source conservation')
        need(all(pin(data[name]) != prior['complete_before'][name] for name in changed),
             'genuine exact two-source repair')
        payload = b'opaque unrelated qualification data\n'
        oid = subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(fixture.root), 'hash-object', '-w', '--stdin'], input=payload).decode().strip()
        names = ['unrelated/' + 'x' * 160 + f'{i:05}.bin' for i in range(20_001)] + ['λ']
        update = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(fixture.root), 'update-index', '--index-info'],
                                input=''.join(f'100644 {oid}\t{name}\n' for name in names).encode(), capture_output=True)
        need(update.returncode == 0 and not update.stdout and not update.stderr, 'real unchanged native opaque population')
        fixture.git('commit', '-q', '-m', 'fixture exact stock inventory population')
        revision = fixture.git('rev-parse', 'HEAD').decode().strip()
        results = []
        for selector in ('index', revision):
            tree = selector != 'index'
            command = ['ls-tree', '-r', '--full-tree', '-z', selector] if tree else ['ls-files', '--stage', '-z']
            wire = fixture.git(*command)
            complete = parse(wire, tree)
            wanted = dict(prior['results'][int(tree)]['complete'])
            for name in changed:
                raw = data[name]
                wanted[name] = ['100644', hashlib.sha1(b'blob ' + str(len(raw)).encode() + b'\0' + raw).hexdigest()]
            need(complete == wanted, 'independent exact prior population with two repaired objects')
            canonical_bytes = sum(len(mode) + 1 + len(object_id) + 3 + len(name.encode()) + 1
                                  for name, (mode, object_id) in complete.items())
            need(canonical_bytes > selected.MAX_INVENTORY_BYTES, 'same genuine native inventory overflow')
            try:
                selected.GitSnapshot(fixture.root, selector)
            except ValueError as error:
                need(str(error) == 'Git output exceeds selected snapshot bound', 'default full API keeps its refusal')
                default_refusal = {'status': 1, 'cause': str(error)}
            else:
                raise ValueError('default full inventory falsely accepted overflow')
            snapshot = published.selected_snapshot(fixture.root, selector,
                                                    bindings=(REGISTRY, AUTHORITIES, 'λ/registry.json'))
            need(snapshot.objects == {p: tuple(v) for p, v in prior['results'][int(tree)]['selected'].items()},
                 'real constructor exactly matches complete independently qualified source domain')
            prepared = published.selected_store(fixture.root, snapshot, False,
                                                published.STORE_SOURCE_SHA256, published.STORE_INDEX_SHA256)
            need(prepared == prior['results'][int(tree)]['prepared'], 'complete old semantic products conserve')
            public = fixture.public('check', selector=selector, installed=True)
            need(public.returncode == 0 and not public.stderr and public.stdout ==
                 b'decision-records: authenticated originals, current records, compatibility and indexes verified\n',
                 'complete repaired installed public result')
            controls = []

                    need(str(error) == cause, 'actual intended scoped read refusal')
                    controls.append({'path': name, 'status': 1, 'cause': cause})
                else:
                    raise ValueError('false green actual scoped read control')

                            'document': selected.catalog_api.MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES,
                            'scope_declarations': selected.catalog_api.MAX_SOURCE_RECORDS},
                 'role': 'Real production constructor and installed public reader on the exact dated stock population; integration closure remains SEM.78.3-owned.'}
    finally:

    print('PASS real production scope and complete unchanged stock population/products; default overflow and scoped read controls refuse.')

import copy
import hashlib
import json
import posixpath
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import types
from pathlib import Path

BASE = Path('docs/audits/decision-index-repair-20261008')
OLD = Path('docs/audits/decision-index-scope-20261008')
ROLE = 'Real production constructor and installed public reader on the exact dated stock population; integration closure remains SEM.78.3-owned.'


def need(condition, cause):
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(cause)


def pin(raw):
    return {'bytes': len(raw), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()}


def parse(raw, tree):
    need(raw.endswith(b'\0'), 'independent complete native wire')
    result = {}
    for record in raw.split(b'\0')[:-1]:
        header, name = record.split(b'\t', 1)
        fields = header.split(b' ')
        need(len(fields) == 3, 'independent exact metadata header')
        mode, oid = fields[0], fields[2] if tree else fields[1]
        need(mode in (b'100644', b'100755', b'120000', b'160000')
             and re.fullmatch(b'[0-9a-f]{40}', oid), 'independent native modes and object identities')
        need(fields[1] == (b'commit' if mode == b'160000' else b'blob') if tree else fields[2] == b'0',
             'independent native object kinds or zero stages')
        path = name.decode()
        need(path not in result, 'independent unique raw path')
        result[path] = [mode.decode(), oid.decode()]
    return result


def size(objects):
    return sum(len(f'{mode} {oid} 0\t{path}\0'.encode()) for path, (mode, oid) in objects.items())


def check(product, expected):
    need(product['role'] == ROLE, 'independent exact qualified scope')
    need(type(product['limits']['inventory']) is int and product['limits'] == expected['limits'],
         'independent unchanged limits')
    need(len(product['results']) == 2, 'independent complete selector population')
    for actual, wanted in zip(product['results'], expected['results']):
        need(actual['complete_wire'] == wanted['complete_wire'], 'independent complete native wire')
        need(actual['objects'] == wanted['objects'], 'independent complete relevant raw-path/mode/object allocation')
        need(type(actual['canonical_bytes']) is int and actual['canonical_bytes'] == wanted['canonical_bytes']
             and type(actual['selected_bytes']) is int and actual['selected_bytes'] == wanted['selected_bytes'],
             'independent actual canonical byte accounting')
        need(actual['prepared'] == wanted['prepared'], 'independent complete semantic products')
        public = actual['public']
        need(type(public['status']) is int and public['status'] == 0 and public['stderr'] == ''
             and public['stdout'] == 'decision-records: authenticated originals, current records, compatibility and indexes verified\n',
             'independent complete actual installed result')
        refusal = actual['default_refusal']
        need(type(refusal['status']) is int and refusal ==
             {'status': 1, 'cause': 'Git output exceeds selected snapshot bound'}, 'independent default refusal')
        need(actual['controls'] == wanted['controls'] and all(type(c['status']) is int and c['status'] == 1
                                                            for c in actual['controls']),
             'independent complete actual scoped controls')

    product = json.loads((BASE / 'proof.json').read_bytes())
    prior = json.loads((OLD / 'proof.json').read_bytes())

         'independent entire immutable diagnosis binding')
    diagnosis = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', str(OLD / 'verify.py')], capture_output=True)
    need(diagnosis.returncode == 0 and not diagnosis.stderr and diagnosis.stdout ==
         product['diagnosis']['actual']['stdout'].encode(), 'independent actual immutable diagnosis execution')
    need(type(product['diagnosis']['actual']['status']) is int
         and product['diagnosis']['actual']['status'] == 0 and not product['diagnosis']['actual']['stderr'],
         'independent complete saved diagnosis receipt')
    for path, row in product['sources'].items():
        raw = row['source'].encode()
        need(row['identity'] == pin(raw) and Path(path).read_bytes() == raw,
             'independent complete programme/source currency')
    fixture_revision = re.search(r"REVISION = '([0-9a-f]{40})'",
                                product['sources']['t/python/test_decision_production_growth.py']['source'])[1]
    data = {name: value.encode() for name, value in product['inputs'].items()}
    need(set(data) == set(prior['complete_before']), 'independent complete input population')
    for path, raw in data.items():
        if path in product['sources']:
            need(raw == product['sources'][path]['source'].encode(), 'independent exact repaired reader input')
        else:
            original = subprocess.check_output(['git', '--no-replace-objects', 'show', fixture_revision + ':' + path])
            need(raw == original, 'independent complete fixed-Git fixture source')
        if path not in ('scripts/decision_records.py', 'scripts/decision_store_git.py'):
            need(pin(raw) == prior['complete_before'][path], 'independent non-repair conservation')
    # Use the captured unchanged semantic source modules, not the scope producer.

    files = {published.CENSUS, 'docs/audits/decision-store-transition-census.json',

        for path, value in complete.items():

            need(value == ['100644', hashlib.sha1(b'blob ' + str(len(raw)).encode() + b'\0' + raw).hexdigest()],
                 'independent every native source/opaque object')
        need(all(complete[path] == ['100644', opaque_oid] for path in opaque), 'independent opaque allocation')
        row['objects'] = {p: v for p, v in complete.items()

        row['canonical_bytes'] = size(complete)
        row['selected_bytes'] = size(row['objects'])
        need(row['canonical_bytes'] > 4_194_304 >= row['selected_bytes'], 'independent genuine whole overflow and bounded selection')
        reader = lambda path: data[path]

                                              published.STORE_INDEX_SHA256, reader=reader)
        old['decision_store'].verify(Path.cwd(), prepared, reader=reader,
                                     paths=tuple(sorted(p for p in row['objects']
                                                        if re.fullmatch('docs/decisions/[^/]+\\.md', p))))
        published.verify(Path.cwd(), prepared, reader=reader)
        need(prepared == prior['results'][number]['prepared'], 'independent original complete semantic conservation')
        row['prepared'] = prepared
        row['controls'] = [{'path': 'λ/registry.json', 'status': 1,
                            'cause': 'selected source has a nondirectory ancestor: λ/registry.json'},
                           {'path': 'unrelated/' + 'x' * 160 + '00000.bin', 'status': 1,
                            'cause': 'selected source is outside declared scope: unrelated/' + 'x' * 160 + '00000.bin'}]
    check(product, expected)

        ('lost-selector', lambda c: c['results'].pop(), 'independent complete selector population'),
        ('integration-promotion', lambda c: c.update(role='All integration and full CI closed.'), 'independent exact qualified scope'),
    ):
        candidate = copy.deepcopy(product)
        mutate(candidate)
        need(json.dumps(candidate, sort_keys=True) != json.dumps(product, sort_keys=True),
             'independent genuine control')
        try:
            check(candidate, expected)
        except ValueError as error:

"""Bounded immutable blob access and catalog continuity for selected gate products."""

import os
import re
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import decision_catalog as catalog_api

MAX_INVENTORY_BYTES = 4_194_304
# Every SHA-1 index record needs mode, object ID, stage, tab, a nonempty
# path and NUL. Committed trees use that same zero-stage representation.
# The default whole-inventory API counts every tracked entry. An explicit
# source scope uses the same cap for its complete selected metadata.
MIN_INVENTORY_RECORD_BYTES = len(b'100644 ' + b'0' * 40 + b' 0\ta\0')
MAX_TRACKED_PATHS = MAX_INVENTORY_BYTES // MIN_INVENTORY_RECORD_BYTES
REGULAR_MODES = ('100644', '100755')


class GitSnapshot:
    """Capture path/mode/object IDs once; never re-read a mutable index selector."""

    def __init__(self, root, selector, *, files=None, subtrees=()):
        self.root = Path(root).resolve(strict=True)
        top = self._git('rev-parse', '--show-toplevel', maximum=4096).decode('utf-8').strip()
        catalog_api.require(Path(top).resolve(strict=True) == self.root,
                            'selected Git root differs from requested repository')
        catalog_api.require(selector in ('index', 'HEAD', 'HEAD^')
                            or type(selector) is str and re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-f]{40}', selector),
                            'unsafe or unsupported Git snapshot selector')
        self.objects = {}
        self.inventory_bytes = 0
        self._files = None
        if files is not None:
            self._set_scope(files, subtrees)
        else:
            catalog_api.require(not subtrees, 'subtrees require an explicit source scope')
        if selector == 'index':
            self.revision = None
        else:
            revision = self._git('rev-parse', '--verify', selector + '^{commit}', maximum=128).decode().strip()
            catalog_api.require(re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-f]{40}', revision), 'unresolved Git snapshot revision')
            self.revision = revision
        if self._files is None:
            listing = (self._git('ls-files', '--stage', '-z', maximum=MAX_INVENTORY_BYTES)
                       if selector == 'index' else
                       self._git('ls-tree', '-r', '--full-tree', '-z', self.revision,
                                 maximum=MAX_INVENTORY_BYTES, tree_inventory=True))
            self._capture(listing, index=selector == 'index')
        else:
            self._capture_scope()
        self.root_paths = tuple(sorted(path for path in self.objects
                                       if re.fullmatch(r'docs/decisions/[^/]+\.md', path)))

    def _set_scope(self, files, subtrees):
        """Declare bounded sources and the metadata needed to reject ancestors."""
        for values in (files, subtrees):
            catalog_api.require(type(values) in (tuple, list)
                                and len(values) <= catalog_api.MAX_SOURCE_RECORDS,
                                'invalid bounded Git source scope')
        paths = list(files) + list(subtrees)
        catalog_api.require(paths and len(paths) <= catalog_api.MAX_SOURCE_RECORDS,
                            'invalid bounded Git source scope')
        parts = {}
        for path in paths:
            value = catalog_api.relative_parts(path)
            parts[path] = value
        catalog_api.require(sum(len(path.encode('utf-8')) + 1 for path in paths)
                            <= catalog_api.MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES, 'Git source scope exceeds byte bound')
        self._files = frozenset(files)
        self._subtrees = tuple(sorted(path for path in set(subtrees)
                                      if not any(path.startswith(parent + '/')
                                                 for parent in subtrees if parent != path)))
        self._ancestors = frozenset('/'.join(value[:length])
                                    for value in parts.values() for length in range(1, len(value)))

    def _in_scope(self, path):
        return path in self._files or any(path == parent or path.startswith(parent + '/')
                                         for parent in self._subtrees)

    @staticmethod
    def _exact_index_pathspec(path):
        # Literal directory names recurse in ls-files. A forced byte class
        # selects only the exact tracked parent/file, including UTF-8 names.
        raw = path.encode('utf-8')
        first = bytes(raw[:1])
        if first in (b'!', b'^', b'-', b']', b'['):
            first = b'\\' + first
        tail = b''.join((b'\\' if byte in b'\\*?[]' else b'') + bytes([byte])
                        for byte in raw[1:])
        return b':(top,glob)[' + first + b']' + tail

    def _capture_scope(self):
        exact = sorted(path for path in self._files | self._ancestors
                       if not any(path == parent or path.startswith(parent + '/')
                                  for parent in self._subtrees))
        if self.revision is None:
            # One index enumeration captures all relevant objects atomically;
            # blob reads below never consult that mutable selector again.
            specs = [':(top,literal)' + path for path in self._subtrees]
            specs.extend(self._exact_index_pathspec(path) for path in exact)
            listing = self._git('ls-files', '--stage', '-z', '--', *specs,
                                maximum=MAX_INVENTORY_BYTES)
            self._capture(listing, index=True)
        else:
            if self._subtrees:
                listing = self._git('ls-tree', '-r', '--full-tree', '-z', self.revision,
                                    '--', *[':(top,literal)' + path for path in self._subtrees],
                                    maximum=MAX_INVENTORY_BYTES, tree_inventory=True)
                self._capture(listing, index=False)
            # ls-tree does not support glob magic. Overlapping parent arguments
            # broaden its output; query each exact path at the same resolved SHA.
            for path in exact:
                listing = self._git('ls-tree', '--full-tree', '-z', self.revision,
                                    '--', ':(top,literal)' + path,
                                    maximum=MAX_INVENTORY_BYTES, tree_inventory=True,
                                    directory_entries=True)
                self._capture(listing, index=False, exact=path)

    def _capture(self, listing, *, index, exact=None):
        records = listing.split(b'\0')
        catalog_api.require(records[-1] == b'' and len(records) - 1 <= MAX_TRACKED_PATHS,
                            'Git path inventory exceeds bound or is incomplete')
        for record in records[:-1]:
            header, path_bytes = record.split(b'\t', 1)
            path = path_bytes.decode('utf-8')
            fields = header.decode('ascii').split(' ')
            if index:
                catalog_api.require(len(fields) == 3 and fields[2] == '0', 'conflicting Git index stages')
                mode, object_id = fields[:2]
            else:
                catalog_api.require(len(fields) == 3 and fields[2] == '0',
                                    'malformed Git tree inventory')
                mode, object_id = fields[:2]
            catalog_api.require(re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-f]{40}', object_id), 'malformed Git object identity')
            if exact is not None:
                catalog_api.require(path == exact, 'Git exact source inventory broadened')
                if mode == '040000':
                    continue  # Full recursive inventories also omit directories.
            if self._files is not None:
                catalog_api.require(self._in_scope(path) or path in self._ancestors,
                                    'Git inventory escapes declared source scope')
            catalog_api.require(path not in self.objects, 'duplicate Git inventory path')
            self.inventory_bytes += len(record) + 1
            catalog_api.require(self.inventory_bytes <= MAX_INVENTORY_BYTES,
                                'Git output exceeds selected snapshot bound')
            catalog_api.require(len(self.objects) < MAX_TRACKED_PATHS,
                                'Git path inventory exceeds bound or is incomplete')
            self.objects[path] = (mode, object_id)

    @staticmethod
    def _read_tree_inventory(stream, maximum, *, directory_entries=False):
        """Bound canonical metadata while preserving standard -z raw paths.

        Standard tree headers carry an object type instead of an index stage.
        Parse bounded chunks and retain the equivalent zero-stage encoding;
        custom Git formatters can quote paths even with -z.
        """
        output = bytearray()
        pending = b''
        while block := stream.read1(65_536):
            records = (pending + block).split(b'\0')
            pending = records.pop()
            for record in records:
                header, separator, path = record.partition(b'\t')
                fields = header.split(b' ')
                catalog_api.require(separator and path and len(fields) == 3,
                                    'malformed Git tree inventory')
                mode, kind, object_id = fields
                expected_kind = (b'tree' if directory_entries and mode == b'040000'
                                 else b'commit' if mode == b'160000' else b'blob')
                catalog_api.require(kind == expected_kind,
                                    'malformed Git tree inventory')
                canonical = mode + b' ' + object_id + b' 0\t' + path + b'\0'
                catalog_api.require(len(output) + len(canonical) <= maximum,
                                    'Git output exceeds selected snapshot bound')
                output.extend(canonical)
            # A commit header is at most five bytes longer than its canonical
            # counterpart. Bound even an incomplete or malformed wire record.
            catalog_api.require(len(output) + len(pending) <= maximum + 5,
                                'Git output exceeds selected snapshot bound')
        catalog_api.require(not pending, 'Git path inventory exceeds bound or is incomplete')
        return bytes(output)

    def _git(self, *arguments, maximum, tree_inventory=False, directory_entries=False):
        # Git metadata/blob commands never recurse into a gitlink. Merge the
        # diagnostic pipe to bound both streams; any successful warning would
        # invalidate the expected metadata or content rather than substitute it.
        environment = {**os.environ, 'GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH': '1', 'GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS': '0'}
        process = subprocess.Popen(['git', '--no-replace-objects', '-C', str(self.root), *arguments],
                                   stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, env=environment)
        try:
            output = (self._read_tree_inventory(process.stdout, maximum,
                                               directory_entries=directory_entries) if tree_inventory
                      else process.stdout.read(maximum + 1))
            if len(output) > maximum:
                process.kill()
                catalog_api.require(False, 'Git output exceeds selected snapshot bound')
            status = process.wait()
            catalog_api.require(status == 0, 'selected Git object cannot be read')
            return output
        finally:
            process.stdout.close()
            if process.poll() is None:
                process.kill()
            process.wait()

    def read(self, path):
        parts = catalog_api.relative_parts(path)
        catalog_api.require(self._files is None or self._in_scope(path),
                            f'selected source is outside declared scope: {path}')
        catalog_api.require(not any('/'.join(parts[:length]) in self.objects
                                    for length in range(1, len(parts))),
                            f'selected source has a nondirectory ancestor: {path}')
        catalog_api.require(path in self.objects, f'unresolved selected source: {path}')
        mode, object_id = self.objects[path]
        catalog_api.require(mode in REGULAR_MODES, f'selected source is not a regular blob: {path}')
        size_bytes = self._git('cat-file', '-s', object_id, maximum=64)
        catalog_api.require(re.fullmatch(rb'[0-9]+\n', size_bytes), 'malformed selected blob size')
        size = int(size_bytes)
        catalog_api.require(size <= catalog_api.MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES, f'selected source exceeds byte bound: {path}')
        data = self._git('cat-file', 'blob', object_id, maximum=catalog_api.MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES)
        catalog_api.require(len(data) == size, 'selected blob size changed')
        return data


def verify_continuity(prior, current):

Knowledge Map (KM) — a derived, question-keyed retrieval layer

A portable, harness-agnostic extension to the Durable Memory Architecture that makes sure an AI/LLM (or a human) never has to do archaeology — re-deriving a fact from code or runtime — to rediscover something that was already logged once.

This file is intentionally project-agnostic: it names no nouns from any one codebase. Drop the knowledge-map/ bundle into any repository that already uses task-trees + MEMORY_ARCHITECTURE.md and it applies as-is.

One-line thesis: durable facts become findable when each is a small, self-describing, front-mattered file, and a machine derives a bounded question-keyed index plus topic shards from them — so retrieval is one query, not an excavation.

0. The problem this solves (and the one it does not)

Teams that already write things down still watch a fresh agent re-derive facts from code. That is archaeology, and it is a retrieval failure, not a recording failure: the fact existed (in a task leaf, a commit message, a decision record) but the next session could not find it, so it dug it out of the source again and — worse — sometimes dressed the re-derivation up as diligence.

Be honest about the ceiling. There are two kinds of “finding a fact”:

  • Re-deriving a fact that was already established (a root cause, an architectural decision, a gotcha). This is the archaeology the KM eliminates.
  • Measuring the current state of a living system for the first time (today’s metric, which case fails right now). You cannot pre-write a measurement you have not taken; this is legitimate diagnostics, not a failure. The KM’s job there is narrow: once measured, its durable conclusion becomes a fact card so nobody measures it twice.

Target: zero archaeology for structural/causal facts; diagnostics only for genuinely-new state, whose conclusions then become facts.

1. Why a derived index (and not a hand-curated one)

A hand-maintained index is the very anti-pattern MEMORY_ARCHITECTURE.md forbids (“prefer derived over hand-written … so it cannot drift”; “hand-maintained current-state that drifts” is an explicit anti-pattern). It also costs time at every commit. So the KM splits the two costs and keeps only the cheap one:

  • Curation cost — a human/agent deciding what to index and phrasing the keys. This is the expensive, rot-prone part. The KM eliminates it: the keys live inside each fact file, authored once, when you write the fact you were recording anyway.
  • Generation cost — a script scanning files and emitting the map. The machine pays it (in the pre-commit hook), never the workflow, never the agent.

The map is a build artifact, never hand-edited, deterministic (sorted, no timestamps) so “regenerate-and-diff” is a valid sync gate. Because the facts are atomic and front-mattered, an agent can also skip the map entirely and grep the fact files directly — the map is a convenience cache, not a load-bearing dependency. (Contrast a hand-index, where staleness breaks everything.)

2. What a fact is

A fact is one .md file whose YAML front-matter has a non-empty answers: list. The presence of answers: is the marker — no separate flag. Required and optional fields:

FieldReq?Purpose
id✅stable, unique, kebab-case identifier (used as the map anchor)
title✅one-line human title
answers✅the questions a future agent will search for, in their words (this is the retrieval surface — list synonyms)
date✅when the fact was established (absolute, YYYY-MM-DD)
evidence or reverify✅ (≥1)what proves it / the cheap command to re-confirm it
reverify⬚a single cheap command that re-establishes the fact (so an agent trusts it, or runs ONE command — never full archaeology)
tags⬚topical tags
status⬚current (default) · superseded · deprecated
supersedes⬚id of the fact this replaces

Front-matter format is a constrained YAML subset parsed without third-party modules: scalars key: value; inline lists key: [a, b]; block lists (key: then - item); and folded >- scalars for long evidence, reverify, or answer values. Folded continuation lines use at least two spaces and are joined with one space. Use plain or double-quoted scalars, never tabs; questions containing a comma use the block-list form. Copy templates/FACT_TEMPLATE.md to start.

3. The six properties LLMs need (why the format is shaped this way)

Humans browse and recognize; LLMs query (grep/semantic) and follow pointers. So:

  1. Query-shaped keys. answers: are phrased as the questions you’d actually grep — not topics a human would skim. Include synonyms and the literal error string.
  2. Canonical vocabulary. One canonical term per concept; list aliases in answers: so any search term routes to the one home. (Grep is lexical — drift loses half the hits.)
  3. Atomic, titled units. One fact per file; the title is the index entry. (A fact buried at line 480 of a 600-line chapter is grep-findable but expensive to read.)
  4. Self-dating + self-verifying. date + evidence + reverify let an agent trust a fact, or re-confirm with one command — instead of re-deriving “to be safe.”
  5. Stable anchors + cross-links. id is a stable anchor; link related facts with [[other-id]] so one lookup leads to its neighbors.
  6. Pointer, not copy. A fact card points to the canonical home (book chapter, code, decision record). The full story stays there; the card makes it findable.

4. What to index — and what NEVER to convert

The KM is additive. You convert nothing. It is a retrieval layer on top of your existing docs, not a replacement. Each existing layer keeps its job; the KM points into it.

LayerRoleKM relationship
mdBooknarrative / teachingdestination — a card’s body links to the chapter
live status / changelogcurrent statenot indexed — changes too fast (it’s not a durable fact)
task-treeswork frontier (layer B)not indexed — a fact that emerges from a task is promoted to a card on conclusion
decision records (layer C)durable ADR factsoptionally add answers: front-matter in place to fold one into the map (zero duplication)
Knowledge Mapretrieval indexderived from the cards above

DO write a card when:

  • you establish a durable, structural/causal fact (a root cause, an architectural constraint, a gotcha, where-something-lives) — i.e. the kind that would otherwise need archaeology; or
  • you catch yourself re-deriving a fact that should already have been written down (write the card then, so it never recurs).

DON’T:

  • ❌ Convert prose docs/the book/task-trees into cards (destroys narrative, duplicates content, goes stale — the §12 anti-pattern).
  • ❌ Hand-edit the generated map. It is derived.
  • ❌ Card a measurement that changes every run (a metric, today’s count). Card the durable conclusion, not the reading.
  • ❌ Card narrative/teaching (book’s job), current status (live-docs’ job), history (git’s job).
  • ❌ Duplicate a fact across cards. One canonical card per fact; supersedes when it changes (don’t silently rewrite).
  • ❌ Omit evidence/reverify — without them an agent re-derives anyway, defeating the purpose.
  • ❌ Put nondeterminism (timestamps) into the map — it breaks the sync gate.

There is no migration project. The map grows one cheap card at a time; each card permanently retires one future archaeology.

5. The scripts and bounded projection

The shell entrypoints use one dependency-free Perl core (Perl 5 core modules only, on BSD/macOS and GNU/Linux):

  • scripts/gen_knowledge_map.sh scans KM_SCAN_DIRS and writes a small KM_OUTPUT landing page plus deterministic topic shards under KM_SHARD_DIR. A topic is the first two kebab-case fact-ID components. Each fact appears in one topic catalog; each unique question appears in one shard and may point to multiple facts when the source cards deliberately share it.
  • scripts/query_knowledge_map.sh performs a case-insensitive fixed- substring search over question rows. Its default cache lives beneath KM_QUERY_CACHE_DIR; --no-cache reads the committed shards directly and --all returns every question row. Cache data is disposable and never owns a fact.
  • scripts/check_knowledge_map.sh rejects missing fields, duplicate IDs, oversized cards/root/shards/aggregate, missing/extra/stale shards, missing or duplicated projected facts/questions, and cached/direct result drift.

gen_knowledge_map.sh --print-map-path, --print-shard-dir, and --print-generated-paths expose hook-safe paths. Config precedence (scripts/knowledge_map.conf, all := assignments) is environment > repo-root .knowledge_map.conf > bundle default. Main knobs are KM_SCAN_DIRS, KM_OUTPUT, KM_SHARD_DIR, KM_QUERY_CACHE_DIR, and KM_TITLE; finite card/projection caps also have KM_*_MAX_* overrides for fixture testing and deliberate adoption calibration.

6. Enforcement — so the map cannot rot

Mirror the four-layer defense from MEMORY_ARCHITECTURE.md §9 (a rule nothing checks is a rule nothing follows):

  • Pre-commit hook regenerates the root and shards, stages both paths with deletion awareness, then runs the check — so the agent spends zero time indexing and the projection is always in sync. See hooks/pre-commit.snippet.
  • CI runs check_knowledge_map.sh (same script) — catches a bypassed hook; a stale map or invalid fact fails the build. See ci/knowledge-map-gate.yml.

Because generation is deterministic, the hook’s “regenerate + stage” makes drift structurally impossible: the committed map always equals what the facts produce.

7. Read path — how a future agent uses it (no archaeology)

  1. From the bootstrap entrypoint, run knowledge-map/scripts/query_knowledge_map.sh 'question words'.
  2. Follow the returned repository-relative canonical card path. Use KNOWLEDGE_MAP.md to browse topic counts or a whole shard when needed.
  3. Trust the fact (it is dated + evidenced), or run its one reverify command.
  4. Only if the fact is genuinely absent is new investigation warranted — and its conclusion becomes a new card before the turn ends.

8. Adoption checklist (any repo already using task-trees + MEMORY_ARCHITECTURE)

  1. Copy the knowledge-map/ bundle into the repo root; commit it.
  2. bash knowledge-map/install.sh (creates docs/knowledge/, generates the first map, prints the hook + CI wiring) — or do those steps by hand from §6.
  3. Add the hook snippet (hooks/pre-commit.snippet) to .githooks/pre-commit; ensure git config core.hooksPath .githooks is set.
  4. Add the CI step (ci/knowledge-map-gate.yml) to your pipeline.
  5. Seed it: write a card for each fact you have recently had to re-derive. Going forward, add a card whenever you establish a durable fact or catch archaeology.
  6. (Optional) fold high-traffic docs/decisions/ records into the map by adding answers: front-matter in place.

9. Anti-patterns (quick reference)

  • ❌ Hand-editing the generated map.
  • ❌ A big-bang “convert all docs to the KM” project.
  • ❌ Letting a root map, topic shard, individual card, or aggregate grow without an independent finite bound.
  • ❌ Cards that duplicate book/prose instead of pointing to it.
  • ❌ Carding volatile metrics instead of durable conclusions.
  • ❌ Cards with no evidence/reverify (agent re-derives anyway).
  • ❌ Nondeterministic map output (breaks the sync gate).
  • ❌ Treating the projection or disposable query cache as load-bearing — facts must stay greppable without either.
  • ❌ An index with no enforcement — it rots.

This bundle is itself an instance of what it describes: small, structured, in-repo, git-tracked, self-describing, and backed by a derive-and-diff gate so it is hard to let it drift. It composes with — and does not replace — MEMORY_ARCHITECTURE.md.
